course.title: Data Preparation at Scale: Contracts, Synthetic Data and Privacy
course.tagline: Contract and link several data producers, prepare 30 million rows idempotently on a laptop, and release health data only after measuring its utility and its risk
course.description: Participants run data preparation for the fictional Rimah Health Data Consortium: three hospital groups send encounter, laboratory and pharmacy extracts (about 30 million synthetic rows) for a readmission study, and a university partner wants a copy. They contract and link the producers, rebuild preparation as an incremental pipeline over partitioned columnar tables, generate and attack synthetic versions, compare privacy-enhancing methods for four requests, and write a release decision a privacy officer could sign. Single-table contracts come from DS-311; de-identification and basic differential privacy from DS-309.
course.audience: Specialists. Data scientists who have completed the level 300 core and practicum, or can show equivalent work: an analysis they led from question to recommendation and defended.
prerequisites: DS-309 Responsible Data Science: Privacy, Fairness and Documentation
Writes SQL with window functions and cleans data with a data-frame library
Has written a data contract and blocking quality rules for one table (DS-311 or equivalent)
Setup: a laptop CPU with uv, or Google Colab. No model and no API key is needed. Run 00_setup_check before Day 1; see labs/README.md.
course.format_note: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task

outcomes.text: Design shared data contracts, a pseudonymous linkage key and a breaking-change policy for a feed with several producers, given three producers whose extracts disagree on schema, codes and units
outcomes.evidence: contracts checked against all three producers, a linkage match rate measured against the planted truth, and a one-page policy

outcomes.text: Implement an incremental, idempotent preparation pipeline over partitioned columnar tables with quality gates, given 30 million synthetic rows on a laptop
outcomes.evidence: identical output when a day is re-run, with time and memory measured

outcomes.text: Evaluate a synthetic dataset for fidelity, analytical utility and disclosure risk, given two generators fitted to related patient and encounter tables
outcomes.evidence: a report with train-on-synthetic, test-on-real scores and attack results

outcomes.text: Compute differentially private statistics under a budget shared across repeated releases, given twelve monthly statistics
outcomes.evidence: a budget ledger and a plot of error against budget

outcomes.text: Select a privacy-enhancing method for each data request by comparing protection, utility and cost, given four requests, from an internal analyst to an external university
outcomes.evidence: a decision table stating the residual risk of each option

outcomes.text: Decide whether to release a dataset and on what conditions, and defend the decision, given the university request and the measured results
outcomes.evidence: a release decision record defended live

case_study.name: Rimah Health Data Consortium
case_study.summary: Rimah Health Data Consortium is a fictional consortium of three hospital groups (Sidra Hospitals, Ufuq Medical Group and Rawdah Hospitals) that send encounter, laboratory and pharmacy extracts for a 30-day readmission study, while a university partner asks for a copy. Participants contract and link the three producers, rebuild preparation as an incremental pipeline over partitioned columnar tables, generate and attack synthetic patient and encounter tables, spend a privacy budget over twelve monthly releases, pool a rate without pooling records, and write the release decision for the university. All data is synthetic, generated with a fixed seed, with planted identifiers and planted problems.

days.label: Capstone
days.title: Capstone: a release package and its defence
days.subtitle: Ten minutes each, questions included: the package, its measured results and one attack re-run live

capstone.summary: A release package for one of three data requests (contracts, pipeline, protected or synthetic dataset with utility and attack report, release decision) in a public repository whose README reports measured results, defended in ten minutes
capstone.submission: A public GitHub repository holding the release package for one of the three requests: the contracts and the pipeline that build the data, the protected or synthetic dataset with its utility and attack report, and the release decision record. Its README reports the measured results with the commands that reproduce them. Then a ten-minute defence, questions included, in which the participant re-runs one attack on a table the assessor chooses.
